storage: append-only JSONL day-files under <archive>/nhtsacomplaints/, one file per FETCH date with event-identity dedup (ODI number) within and across restarts; gz after 2 days
written_by: server/nhtsaComplaints.ts archiveNewComplaints (12h watchlist sweep, ~20 politeness-spaced calls/cycle, eager boot)
source: NHTSA ODI complaints API (api.nhtsa.gov/complaints/complaintsByVehicle) — keyless JSON, US government public domain. Polled over a CURATED ticker-mapped make/model/year watchlist (datacore/nhtsa_vehicles.json, static import) because the daily bulk FLAT_CMPL.zip is 84+MB and unbootable; the bulk file is the documented deep-history follow-up. Shape verified live 2026-07-06; dates arrive MM/DD/YYYY (normalized to ISO)
license: US government work, public domain; attribution 'NHTSA Office of Defects Investigation'

field_map.odi — event-identity dedup key: ODI complaint number; the same complaint never re-archives regardless of fetch windows
field_map.ticker/make/model/model_year: watchlist mapping (ticker is OUR join key, not NHTSA data)
field_map.components: affected components verbatim — the supplier-mapping raw material (Everything Graph follow-up)
field_map.summaries: free text deliberately NOT archived — the velocity signal needs counts/flags/dates, and bulk text belongs to the flat-file follow-up

confidence_model: RAW official complaint events over a curated watchlist — coverage is the WATCHLIST, not the full vehicle universe (stated on the route). The complaint-velocity hypothesis stays gate-locked: gate 1 = counts vs NHTSA's published recall timeline for 3 known cases; gate 2 = velocity anomalies vs forward returns.
cadence: bulk source updates daily; 12h watchlist sweep (~20 calls) makes quiet days dedup no-ops
_note: Universal archive envelope (approved 2026-07-04). BUILD ORDER 6 #4; the wikiAttention curated-seed pattern applied to NHTSA.
